headline: One year later: DU halls still lack uniform emergency care after Liza's death
summary: Despite the tragedy of a student's death, Dhaka University residential halls remain without a standardized emergency medical system.
details: A year has passed since the death of Dhaka University student Liza, highlighting a persistent gap in emergency care within the university's residential halls.
The lack of uniform emergency medical services across different halls has left students vulnerable to sudden health crises.
While some halls may have basic facilities, there is no standardized system to ensure every student receives immediate care during an emergency.
The situation raises critical questions about the university administration's urgency in implementing a comprehensive health safety net for residents.
Students and advocates are calling for a permanent, uniform medical infrastructure to prevent future tragedies.
The continued absence of these facilities underscores the systemic failure to protect student wellbeing in the university's largest residential complexes.

headline: Outsourcing worker gets bail in PMO red telephone cable theft
summary: Ranjan Chandra, accused of stealing copper cables from the Prime Minister's Office, has been granted bail by a Dhaka court.
details: A Dhaka court has granted bail to Ranjan Chandra, a 26-year-old outsourcing worker, in a case involving the theft of copper cables from the Prime Minister's Office (PMO).
The court of Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge-6, Md. Sadekeen Habib, granted bail on a bond of 10,000 BDT on Thursday.
The theft occurred between May 22 and June 1, when approximately 110 meters of BTCL copper cables were stolen from the roofs of old buildings 1, 2, and 3 of the Bangladesh Secretariat.
The stolen cables, used for the red telephone connection, used to have a market value of approximately 105,000 BDT.
Police arrested Ranjan Chandra and a scrap dealer, Rizakul Islam, from the Secretariat area on June 4, using CCTV footage and IT tools.

During initial questioning, Ranjan reportedly confessed to the theft and stated he sold the copper extracted from the cables to a scrap shop called 'Messers Bhai Bhai Traders' near Dhaka University's Ekushey Hall.
Based on this information, Mahabub Hasan, the buyer of the stolen copper, was also arrested. All three suspects had been in jail since their arrest.

Copper cables from the PMO's red telephone connection were stolen and sold to a scrap shop. One of the accused has now been granted bail.

The theft occurred between May 22 and June 1, when approximately 110 meters of BTCL copper cables were stolen from the roofs of old buildings 1, 2, and 3 of the Bangladesh Secretariat.

The stolen cables, used for the red telephone connection, used to have a market value of approximately 105,000 BDT.

Police arrested Ranjan Chandra and a scrap dealer, Rizakul Islam, from the Secretariat area on June 4, using CCTV footage and IT tools.

During initial questioning, Ranjan reportedly confessed to the theft and stated he sold the copper extracted from the cables to a scrap shop called 'Messers Bhai Bhai Traders' near Dhaka University's Ekushey Hall.

Based on this information, Mahabub Hasan, the buyer of the stolen copper, was also arrested. All three suspects had been in jail since their arrest.
